On this project (Helm One / SF32LB52 my_vendor) the working loop is: **the user flashes their own image and
pastes the serial capture; I read it and change code.** Stated verbatim 2026-09-18 while I was quoting an
image size: 「我的boot带了CRC，我烧录的是这个，看构建日期」.

**Why it matters:** every claim of the form "the fix is verified" depends on *which* image produced the log,
and my previous identity for that — `payload_len` / `image_len` / `md5` — cannot work, because the user's
tool rebuilds from the current tree (a clean rebuild lands tens-to-hundreds of bytes away from my
incremental build of the same sources). The discriminator is the 2SFBL banner's **`build_date`**
(`version / build_date / image_len / payload_len`); alignment = **user's build_date > my last edit time**.
Mechanics, the addresses that shift between builds, and the comparison table are in
[[myvendor-git-and-change-tracking]].

**How to apply:**

- **Ask for the banner first** whenever a capture is used to judge a change; without it, say out loud that
  the image is unidentified instead of guessing.
- **Stamp the deliverable**: when handing over a change, name the wall-clock time of the last edit, so the
  banner can be checked against it later.
- **Keep the distinction honest**: "recovery/wedge did not recur" is *unverified*, not fixed — with an
  intermittent trigger, one clean boot proves nothing (the same rule as [[myvendor-sd-card-failure]]'s
  "do not treat one clean boot as a fix"). The one time the log did prove a fix landed was when the new
  instrumentation's own line appeared (`eph skip same src`), not when a failure merely failed to appear.
- **Keep an owed-verification list** rather than letting these blur into "done" — right now it contains the
  reader-zombie release, the watchdog clip-guard, the h4 bounded-reopen path, and MTP's deferred-free path.
  **Worked example (2026-09-18 16:03, `build_date 202609181603`):** that boot was the first flash carrying
  the anti-starvation pair and it came up with both links, no cycle, no wedge — the tempting reading is
  "fixed". It is not: the proof is that **the zombie branch's own line (`zombie released …`) never appeared**,
  because no wedge happened. Only instrumentation that fires on the failure can close an item.
- **Anti-starvation gates ARE now field-verified, and the counter-example is instructive** (2026-09-18 16:24
  and 16:27 boots): the new visibility line `adv active` appeared (so "no advertising" is no longer a
  mystery), the deferral line printed **only** in its in-cycle form, and the 4 s `cmdsilent` escalated to a

  summarising a session as "improved".

    syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[epic] wait timeout +%u (total=%u)\n",

**Semantics the user asked for (their wording: "ctrl q 时恢复需要上屏，保存到 tmp 的文件可以删掉，

screen** in order and then live output continues. Bounded by `MONITOR_PAUSE_MAX` (1 MiB, drops the
OLDEST — keeps the tail contiguous with the live stream) and written out in
`MONITOR_PAUSE_CHUNK` (4 KiB) slices so the port keeps being drained during catch-up. The replay
runs in the **reader** thread (`_pause_service()` at the top of the loop) so ordering is trivially
correct; that in turn required a bounded read wait — `MONITOR_READ_TIMEOUT_S = 0.2` — otherwise the
replay waits for the next incoming byte (an infinite-timeout `read()` was the first symptom).

writer thread blocks in its very first `console.getkey()` call, and that pre-patch call swallows the
first key pressed after startup (it cost a full debug cycle: the key arrived, the handler never ran);

anything yet) and handed over a boot log for analysis instead of accepting an offered fix.

**Why:** the tree contains several plausible failure chains, and first-pass static analysis pointed at
two of them that the hardware log then showed were **not** active — GPS counters were clean
(`bad=0 junk=0 ubx=0 wr_fail=0`) and the BT disconnects were reason 0x13 (peer-initiated), not 0x08.
Diagnosing from real logs before editing is what caught that.

**How to apply:** present the assessment together with the specific log fingerprints that would confirm
or falsify each hypothesis, and let the user choose which fix to start with; do not begin editing until
they say so. When a log contradicts an earlier finding, say so explicitly and re-rank the priorities
rather than defending the earlier analysis. See [[myvendor-gnss-bt-intermittent]] and
[[myvendor-bringup-log-decoding]].

The preference recurs later the same day, twice: first "先不要直接改逻辑…增加更多日志来抓取问题"
(add more logging to catch it, don't change thresholds yet), then a request for a **stress-test
command** (`ctl dvfs hop`, hop the clock every 10 s) rather than a speculative fix. So for this
project: when a fault is intermittent, offer instrumentation plus a way to reproduce or stress it,
keep the change surface additive where possible, and state plainly when a scan or gate blocks a write
instead of quietly working around it.

A third recurrence names the escalation explicitly: **"排查原因，排查不出就加log"** — investigate the
cause, and if you cannot pin it, add logging. So when the evidence runs out, the expected move is to
say which parts are confirmed, say precisely what is *not* pinned, and instrument that gap; it is
**not** to turn an unresolved clue into a speculative fix. In that instance a `g_fs_wake` address was
identified but ruled not-actionable (it contradicted the waiter's timeout semantics, and BLE was
provably healthy), and the working `companion_fs` path was deliberately left untouched — the user has
since confirmed that call.

Same instruction also licenses fixing what the log has already **proven**, without waiting for the
still-open root cause: the unbounded `pthread_join` (468 s of wedged diag) was fixed in the same pass
that added the logging.

**Working rhythm (2026-09-17):** faults arrive as **pasted console logs**, often a pair labelled
「异常1」/「异常2」, with a short instruction like "你看看怎么修复". The user then decides: they
**build and flash themselves** ("我来构建") and hand the resulting boot log straight back, and
"你进行操作吧" is the authorization to implement a proposed instrumentation plan. So the loop is
propose → they flash → paste → refine, and instrumentation is expected to be *inspectable from a
boot log* rather than requiring a debugger.

spent optimising a ~1000-iteration/s loop that turned out to be byte-driven by design, with the

suspect (`busy > win` was arithmetic proof the accumulator was broken), the right move is to say so
and fix the measurement — not to optimise the hot path on it. The user is explicitly fine with
"this line of investigation is closed"; what they do not want is a fix built on a number nobody
